issue.title: Bug: `stress/test_stress_routes.py` fails on multi-asic with `Usage: /usr/bin/vtysh -n [0 to 1] [OPTION]...`

failure.body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Medium

### Description of the bug

	 E           tests.common.errors.RunAnsibleModuleFail: run module shell failed, Ansible Results =>
	 E           failed = True
	 E           changed = True
	 E           rc = 1
	 E           cmd = vtysh -c "show memory bgpd"
	 E           start = 2025-04-27 <IPV6>.869391
	 E           end = 2025-04-27 <IPV6>.882943
	 E           delta = <IPV6>.013552
	 E           msg = non-zero return code
	 E           invocation = {'module_args': {'_raw_params': 'vtysh -c "show memory bgpd"', '_uses_shell': True, 'warn': False, 'stdin_add_newline': True, 'strip_empty_ends': True, 'argv': None, 'chdir': None, 'executable': None, 'creates': None, 'removes': None, 'stdin': None}}
	 E           _ansible_no_log = None
	 E           stdout =
	 E           stderr =
	 E           Usage: /usr/bin/vtysh -n [0 to 1] [OPTION]...

In https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/14240 a couple calls to `vtysh` were added without considering multi-asic systems.

### Steps to Reproduce

Run `stress/test_stress_routes.py` on a multi-asic system

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

Tests should consider the namespace when making `vtysh` calls

### Relevant log output

```shell

```

### Output of `show version`

```shell

```

### Attach files (if any)

_No response_

resolution.title: Handle multi-asic systems in `get_frr_daemon_memory_usage`
resolution.description:
Without this change `stress/test_stress_routes.py` will fail on multi-asic systems with:
